paragraphs.heading: A ring of coral
paragraphs.text: An atoll is an island shaped like a ring: a rim of coral that surrounds a lagoon. Small coral islands, or cays, may sit on the rim. In most atolls the dry land is only a small part of the total area. The islands are low, rising less than 5 metres above the sea.

paragraphs.heading: Where atolls are found
paragraphs.text: Reef-building corals thrive only in warm tropical and subtropical seas, so that is the only place atolls occur. Of roughly 440 atolls in the world, most lie in the Pacific, in groups such as the Marshall Islands, Kiribati and Tuvalu, or in the Indian Ocean, including the Maldives. The Atlantic has no large groups of them, apart from eight atolls east of Nicaragua in the Caribbean.

paragraphs.heading: Darwin's sinking island
paragraphs.text: In 1842 Charles Darwin explained atolls using what he had seen on the voyage of HMS Beagle. A coral fringing reef forms around a volcanic island. Over geologic time the volcano dies, wears away and sinks below the waves, while the reef turns into a barrier reef cut off from the island. In the end only the reef and its small islets remain, with a lagoon where the volcano once stood, though the lagoon is not the old crater. For the atoll to last, the coral must grow fast enough to match the sinking island or the rising sea.

paragraphs.heading: A second explanation
paragraphs.text: Another idea is called the antecedent karst model. First, a flat-topped coral mound forms as an island sinks below sea level. When the sea later falls, the mound is left in the open air, and rain dissolves it into limestone karst. The middle dissolves fastest and the rim slowest, leaving a saucer with a raised edge. When the sea rises again, coral regrows on the rim to make the islands, and the flooded centre becomes the lagoon.

paragraphs.heading: Where the word comes from
paragraphs.text: The word atoll comes from atholhu in Dhivehi, an Indo-Aryan language of the Maldives. It reached French as atollon in 1625. Darwin later used it to mean a circular group of coral islets.

paragraphs.heading: Record holders
paragraphs.text: The northernmost atoll is Kure Atoll at 28°25′ N, in the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands. The southernmost are Elizabeth Reef and Middleton Reef in the Tasman Sea. Aranuka in Kiribati sits closest to the Equator, its southern tip only 13 km north of it. Huvadhu Atoll in the Maldives has the most islands, 255 in all.
